div.head: Rect 4.6
div.ab: [4.6] Hede se ðe scire healde, þæt he wite á, hwæt ealdlandræden sy 7 hwæt ðeode ðeaw.
Uideat qui scyram tenet, ut semper sciat, que sit antiqua terrarum institutio uel populi consuetudo.
On suman ealugafol . hede se ðe scire healde þæt he wite a hwæt ealdland ræden sy . 7 hwæt ðeode ðeaw.
In some estates ale-rent. He that would hold a shire should heed that he know what the old estate customs and what the customs of the region are.
Achte [vgl. Ger. 2. 18] wer das [Gutsvogtei]amt inne hat, dass er stets wisse, was [echte] alte Gutsordnung und was Landesgewohnheit ist!
Let him who holds the [reeve's] office take heed that he always knows what the [true] ancient estate-custom is and what the custom of the people!
div.note: B repeats ‘eald landræden sy ⁊ hwæt’ (a mistaken repetition of the line). Liebermann compares Gerefa 2 and 18.
